summary: Live engine gauges on the iDrive 6 screen: boost, AFR, timing and more
author: inotbarnacle (packaged by NBTApps)
description:
A page of live engine gauges under My Vehicle, read from the car's own control units.

What it does
- Nine gauge positions, which show at first boost, AFR, ignition timing, intake air temperature, transmission temperature, rail pressure, oil pressure, coolant temperature and ethanol content (E%)
- Configure gauges, under OPTIONS → BoostDeck settings, sets the reading of each position, from more such as oil temperature, control module voltage, RPM, load, air flow and fuel rate. A reading the car does not give shows as a dash
- Engine profile, in the same menu, switches to a diesel profile. Gasoline and diesel each keep their own gauge choices
- OPTIONS → BoostDeck settings sets the pressure (psi, bar or kPa), speed (mph or km/h) and temperature (°F or °C) units each on their own, the gauge colour, Multicolor among them, and bars or circular dials
- Alerts, each off at first: a coolant or oil temperature above a limit from 220 to 260 °F, or an oil pressure below one from 5 to 25 psi. Alert mode shows them on the screen only, or with a soft chime too. They use fresh readings while the page is open
- The settings, alerts, engine profile and gauge choices are kept across restarts of iDrive, and go when the package is removed

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6), on a software version the app was built for (see Good to know)
- NBTApps agent 1.6.0 or later
- The car's diagnostic gateway. The app tries 169.254.21.3, and if nothing answers there, looks for the gateway on the car's wired network

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open My Vehicle and choose BoostDeck.

Good to know
- The readings are set up for the first-generation B58 engine; the author's car is a 340i. On another engine some of them may stay blank
- The page is laid out for the screen when the package is installed. An 800×480 or 960×480 screen gets a layout of its own. A 1280×480, 1440×540 or 1920×720 screen gets the 1280×480 layout, which the head unit scales to fit. If the screen's size cannot be read, the 1280×480 layout is used
- On NBTevo_R19144I, owners report that the iDrive screen freezes with BoostDeck and ShiftDeck
- Owners report that on some cars the app only gets data while a device is plugged into the OBD port
- This package does not check the head unit's software version. The author's own installer checks the head unit's iDrive framework files, and accepts those of these NBTevo versions only: K17052I, L17252I, M17345I, M17365I, N18032I, N18092I, O18184I, P18362I, Q18491I, R19101I, R19144I, S19221I, S19322I, T18501I, T21424I, T23235J, T24081I, U19384I, V20153I, W20204I, X20511I, Y21432J, Y22292I, Y23236I and Y24073J. On another version the menu may not load
- If the app was put on this car before, with the author's desktop installer or by hand, uninstall it the same way first. NBTApps refuses to install over it
- If the app does not find the car's diagnostic gateway, put its address in a gateway-ip.txt file on the head unit: /var/opt/hmi/data/ID5/gateway-ip.txt for all of the author's apps at once, or one in the app's own folder. The shared file comes first. This package writes neither
- This is a pre-release: the package has not yet been installed on a car through NBTApps

BoostDeck is by inotbarnacle, free of charge under the MIT License. NBTApps packages the author's own builds, unchanged, with the author's agreement. It comes as it is: you install it at your own risk.
